I like it. It creates an accountability system for the mods.

But what about the admins? Wouldn't their own biases get in the way? We already have seen with reddit how the admins share the same views with SRS and allow them to do the abusive things they do. They could just ignore the reports.

I think it would give more power to the witch hunt against corrupt moderators. Whenever Reddit bans someone new, or there's a fresh resurgence of the SJW red scare here, people start getting paranoid about the moderators. Give them this, and they'll spam it against people who are "too SJW", or whoever they've got the pitchforks out for at the time. I'm certain they would abuse it.

However, it would have its uses. I think it would be better to have a drop down listing the current mods, instead of letting them fill out the name manually. That's just convenient. It would also have to have at least one "Are you certain?" double check; calling a mod corrupt is a fairly serious allegation. It would be most unfortunate if someone accidentally clicked the wrong moderator's name and sent it off without realising.

You'd also have to determine those factors properly; you've listed ideas for them, but not anything specific, or even rough. There should probably also be some rough idea for what they can report them on. I'd think the easiest one would be three or so like "Banning Dissent, Deleting Too Much, Bad Attitude for a Mod, and then Other. Other would give you a box to write something more specific in, or you could have it do that, but also be extra information if you clicked something else.

I think if it comes out that a mod is supposedly bad, there would also need to be a counter system. A way to contest it. Obviously, there's the modlog if you want to try and prove it, or disprove it as the case may be, but what about others? People will reporta mod they think is abusive, but they wouldn't do anything about a good mod because it's the norm. How could you measure the amount of users who don't think the moderator in question is corrupt? I think there would need to be a way to measure that, too. Otherwise you run the risk of creating a false impression that everyone is in agreement when it's just not the case.

I agree with the idea but implementing something like it would be pretty hard. There's a lot of things to account for when it comes to something that people can easily abuse. Only time will tell if Voat as a whole will need and implement it.

On what basis are reports measured? How are the admins expected to reach a decision? What criteria are there for them taking action, or deciding not to? If the site's moderation just becomes a list of people atko agrees with, then it's not too different to reddit.

It's not a better idea, because requiring admin or "supermod" intervention is a non-starter. That system effectively already exists and it is what the other site is doing as well. It doesn't work.

What we need is to put power in the hands of the contributors.
